purpose: record what B/S and C really see so the paper does not call the alignment exact original-pixel co-registration

b_s_convention.resize: torchvision Resize(448, BICUBIC, antialias=True) preserves the aspect ratio and maps the smaller edge to 448
b_s_convention.crop: image_tensor[:, :cropped_height, :cropped_width] -> top-left crop to a multiple of patch size 14
b_s_convention.consequence: the scoring canvas is the cropped tensor, so at most 13 px per axis of the resized image are discarded before patchification

c_convention.resize: the whole image is squashed to a square 518x518 (aspect ratio is lost)
c_convention.grid: 37x37 patch grid in the squashed coordinates
c_convention.regrid: bilinear F.interpolate to B's canvas grid at scoring time, i.e. an approximate normalised alignment, not an exact original-pixel map

mask_convention.rule: ground-truth masks are resized to the same canvas (grid x 14) with NEAREST
mask_convention.consequence: mask-to-patch alignment is exact *on the cropped canvas*; it is not exact with respect to the uncropped original image

measured_cases.crop_convention: top-left crop to a multiple of patch size 14 (torchvision Resize preserves the aspect ratio; smallest edge -> 448)

required_wording: 写「在共同裁剪画布上按归一化坐标对齐」；不得写「原图逐像素严格同位」。C 分支因方形化输入而损失长宽比，只能称近似归一化对齐。
verdict: B/S are exact on the cropped canvas (top-left crop, at most 13 px discarded); C is an approximate normalised alignment because its input is squashed to a square before patchification
